items.title: School Daze
items.line: Spike Lee's second feature opened on February 12, 1988, set at a Black college in Atlanta over homecoming weekend. It cost $6.1 million and took $14.5 million, and E.U.'s 'Da Butt' from it went to number one on the R&B chart.

items.title: Yo! MTV Raps
items.line: MTV aired the US pilot on August 6, 1988, hosted by Run-DMC, with DJ Jazzy Jeff & the Fresh Prince as first guests. Fab 5 Freddy took over as host, and the show ran until August 1995.

items.title: Ben Johnson in Seoul
items.line: On September 24, 1988, Ben Johnson won the Olympic 100 metres in a world-record 9.79 seconds. His sample tested positive for stanozolol and he lost the gold medal and the record days later.

items.title: Super Mario Bros. 3
items.line: Nintendo released it in Japan on October 23, 1988. Americans waited until February 1990, and it sold more than 17 million copies worldwide by 2000.

items.title: The Morris worm
items.line: Cornell graduate student Robert Tappan Morris launched a self-copying program from MIT's network at 8:30 p.m. on November 2, 1988. It is usually said to have hit about 6,000 Unix machines, and he became the first person convicted of a felony under the 1986 Computer Fraud and Abuse Act.

items.title: Bush beats Dukakis
items.line: On November 8, 1988, George H. W. Bush won the presidency with 426 electoral votes and 53.4 percent of the vote to Michael Dukakis's 111. Republican ads about a Massachusetts prison furlough painted Dukakis as soft on crime and were accused of race-baiting.
